16746-inquiries-and-opinions.title: Inquiries And Opinions
16746-inquiries-and-opinions.creator: Unknown
16746-inquiries-and-opinions.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Now that the century in which we were born and bred is receding swiftly into the past, we can perceive in the perspective more clearly than ever before its larger movements and its main endeavor. We are at last beginning to be able to estimate the heritage it has left us, and to see for ourselves what our portion is, what our possessions are, and what our obligations.

arxiv-2209-12660.title: MARLUI: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive UIs CCS: Human-centered computing Graphical user interfaces CCS: Human-centered computing User models CCS: Human-centered computing HCI theory, concepts and models
arxiv-2209-12660.creator: Thomas Langerak, Sammy Christen, Mert Albaba, Christoph Gebhardt, Otmar Hilliges
arxiv-2209-12660.description: Abstract . Adaptive user interfaces (UIs) automatically change an interface to better support users’ tasks. Recently, machine learning techniques have enabled the transition to more powerful and complex adaptive UIs. However, a core challenge for adaptive user interfaces is the reliance on high-quality user data that has to be collected offline for each task.

arxiv-2309-14762.title: GH-convergence of CAT ( 0 ) (0) -spaces: stability of the Euclidean factor
arxiv-2309-14762.creator: Nicola Cavallucci
arxiv-2309-14762.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nicola Cavallucci. We prove that if a sequence of geodesically complete CAT ( 0 ) (0) -spaces X j X_{j} with uniformly cocompact discrete groups of isometries converges in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense to X ∞ X_{\infty} , then the dimension of the maximal Euclidean factor splitted off by X ∞ X_{\infty} and X j X_{j} is the same, for j j big enough. In other words, no additional Euclidean factors can appear in the limit.

arxiv-2405-02560.title: A Pilot Study on the Comparison of Prefrontal Cortex Activities of Robotic Therapies on Elderly with Mild Cognitive Impairment
arxiv-2405-02560.creator: King Tai Henry Au-Yeung, William Wai Lam Chan, Kwan Yin Brian Chan, Hongjie Jiang *, and Junpei Zhong *
arxiv-2405-02560.description: Abstract Demographic shifts have led to an increase in mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and this study investigates the effects of cognitive training (CT) and reminiscence therapy (RT) conducted by humans or socially assistive robots (SARs) on prefrontal cortex activation in elderly individuals with MCI, aiming to determine the most effective therapy-modality combination for promoting cognitive function.

arxiv-2405-07031.title: Global Motion Understanding in Large-Scale Video Object Segmentation
arxiv-2405-07031.creator: Volodymyr Fedynyak, Yaroslav Romanus, Oles Dobosevych, Igor Babin, Roman Riazantsev
arxiv-2405-07031.description: Abstract In this paper, we show that transferring knowledge from other domains of video understanding combined with large-scale learning can improve robustness of Video Object Segmentation (VOS) under complex circumstances. Namely, we focus on integrating scene global motion knowledge to improve large-scale semi-supervised Video Object Segmentation.

arxiv-2409-20256.title: Combining physics-based and data-driven predictions for quantitatively accurate models that extrapolate well; with application to DIII-D, AUG, and ITER tokamak fusion reactors
arxiv-2409-20256.creator: J. Abbate, E. Fable, G. Tardini, R. Fischer, E. Kolemen, ASDEX Upgrade Team
arxiv-2409-20256.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by J. Abbate, E. Fable, G. Tardini, R. Fischer, E. Kolemen, ASDEX Upgrade Team. Methodologies for combining the accuracy of data-driven models with extrapolability of physics-based models are described and tested, for the task of building transport models of tokamak fusion reactors that extrapolate well to new operational regimes. Information from multiple physics simulations (the ASTRA transport code with gyro-Bohm and TGLF estimates for turbulent diffusion) as well as multiple distinct experiments (DIII-D and AUG tokamaks) are considered.

arxiv-2412-05442.title: The Temperature versus Orbital Period relation of AM CVns: Insights from their Donors
arxiv-2412-05442.creator: Colin W. Macrie, Liliana Rivera Sandoval, Yuri Cavecchi, Tin Long Sunny Wong, Manuel Pichardo Marcano
arxiv-2412-05442.description: Abstract We studied the spectral energy distribution (SED) of 22 known AM CVns with orbital periods ( P o ​ r ​ b P_{orb} ) larger than 35 min using multiwavelength public photometric data to estimate the effective temperature of the accreting white dwarf.

arxiv-2511-03468.title: Resonant states reveal strong light-matter coupling in nanophotonic cavities
arxiv-2511-03468.creator: Jan David Fischbach, Sergei Gladyshev, Adrià Canós Valero, Markus Nyman, Thomas Weiss, Carsten Rockstuhl
arxiv-2511-03468.description: Abstract Photonic resonances are a powerful tool for controlling light-matter interactions. However, unlocking many of the most scientifically intriguing and technologically promising phenomena requires entering the strong coupling regime, where light and matter fully mix, unlocking emergent properties of the coupled states.

pmc-10627041.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). esponse to the needs of healthcare systems and societal expectations. pmc-10672128.title: Numerical Simulation of Dynamic Degradation and Fatigue Damage of Degradable Zinc Alloy Stents
pmc-10672128.creator: Jing Qi, Hanbing Zhang, Shiliang Chen, Tianming Du, Yanping Zhang, Aike Qiao
pmc-10672128.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Current research on the fatigue properties of degradable zinc alloy stents has not yet considered the issue of the fatigue life changing with material properties during the dynamic degradation process. Therefore, in this paper, we established a fatigue damage algorithm to study the fatigue problem affected by the changing of material properties during the dynamic degradation process of the stent under the action of pulsating cyclic loading.

pmc-11525784.title: Biosynthetic enzyme analysis identifies a protective role for TLR4-acting gut microbial sulfonolipids in inflammatory bowel disease
pmc-11525784.creator: Ethan A. Older, Jian Zhang, Zachary E. Ferris, Dan Xue, Zheng Zhong, Mary K. Mitchell, Michael Madden, Yuzhen Wang, Hexin Chen, Prakash Nagarkatti, Mitzi Nagarkatti, Daping Fan, Melissa Ellermann, Yong-Xin Li, Jie Li
pmc-11525784.description: The trillions of microorganisms inhabiting the human gut are intricately linked to human health. While specific microbes have been associated with diseases, microbial abundance alone cannot reveal the molecular mechanisms involved. One such important mechanism is the biosynthesis of functional metabolites. Here, we develop a biosynthetic enzyme-guided disease correlation approach to uncover microbial functional metabolites linked to disease.

pmc-11738119.title: Understanding Issues Faced by West Midlands’ International Medical Graduates (IMG) Psychiatry Trainees and How to Support them
pmc-11738119.creator: Supriya Dastidar, Oluwadamilola Ogunsina, Asma Javed
pmc-11738119.description: AimsThe GMC 2023 workforce report indicates that doctors with primary medical qualification (PMQ) outside United Kingdom (UK) made up 62% of new additions to the register in 2022, with international medical graduates (IMGs) from outside the European Economic Area accounting for a further 10%. In 2023, 49.8% of psychiatry trainees in West Midlands were IMGs.

pmc-12382764.title: Spatial Risk Distribution of Lumpy Skin Disease in Thailand Based on Maximum-Entropy Modeling
pmc-12382764.creator: Kusnul Yuli Maulana, Supitchaya Siriyakhun, Kannika Na-Lampang, Kannikar Intawong, Kenny Oriel A Olana, Wengui Li, Maytawee Tamprateep, Veerasak Punyapornwithaya, Giovanni Franzo
pmc-12382764.description: Simple SummaryControlling lumpy skin disease (LSD) in livestock requires more than understanding its biology, it demands insight into where and why outbreaks occur. This study applied the maximum-entropy-modeling approach to LSD outbreak data from 2021 to 2023 in Thailand, integrating environmental variables such as land cover, normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), cattle density, and climate factors.

pmc-12553575.title: Development of a machine learning-based prediction model for acute kidney injury associated with respiratory failure in the intensive care unit
pmc-12553575.creator: Huayang Qin, Qimeng Wu, Jiaxiong Tan, Xiaoxin Tong, Haifang Zhang, Yuping Yang, Weicheng Lai, Ge Song, Shenshen Du
pmc-12553575.description: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and severe complication in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with respiratory failure, associated with high mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial healthcare burden. Conventional risk scores, such as SOFA and APACHE II, are not optimized for AKI prediction in this heterogeneous population.

pmc-12585600.title: Naturally ornate RNA homo-oligomeric complexes
pmc-12585600.creator: Rachael Kretsch, Yuan Wu, Svetlana A Shabalina, Hyunbin Lee, Grace Nye, Eugene V Koonin, Alex Gao, Wah Chiu, Rhiju Das
pmc-12585600.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Myriad families of natural RNAs have been proposed, but not yet experimentally shown, to form biologically important structures. Cryogenic electron microscopy revealed the three-dimensional structures of three large ornate bacterial RNAs at 2.9-3.1 Å. Without precedent among previously characterized natural RNA molecules, Giant, Ornate, Lake- and Lactobacillales-Derived (GOLLD), Rumen-Originating, Ornate, Large (ROOL), and Ornate Large Extremophilic (OLE) RNAs form homo-oligomeric complexes whose stoichiometries are retained at concentrations lower than expected in the cell.

pmc-12729806.title: Biofortification as a sustainable strategy to address micronutrient malnutrition in South Asia
pmc-12729806.creator: Aneesha VijayaKumar, Irshaan Syed, Harshavardhan Dhulipalla, Payel Ghosh, Laxmikarthika V. Srinivasan, Faraz Ahmad, Sandeep Singh Rana, Vipin Singh
pmc-12729806.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Malnutrition is a significant public health concern affecting many populations, particularly in developing countries such as India and its neighboring economies. It can lead to adverse health outcomes, including stunted growth, impaired cognition, and increased susceptibility to disease. This review attempts to summarize the problems associated with malnutrition in different age groups in India and its neighboring countries, and the accompanying factors contributing to it.

pmc-12788528.title: Comparative Study of Chlorhexidine-Loaded Microneedle Patches vs Gels in Local Periodontal Therapy
pmc-12788528.creator: Zakiah Khalid Barri, Abdulmalik Marwan Khateeb, Abdulaziz Awwadh Alqurayqiri, Abdulaziz Khalid Enayah
pmc-12788528.description: Background:Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease, requires effective local antimicrobial therapy. Chlorhexidine (CHX) is a gold-standard antimicrobial, but conventional gel delivery faces limitations in sustained release and pocket penetration.Materials and Methods:A randomized, controlled, single-blind clinical trial was conducted with 60 periodontitis patients (30 per group).

pmc-13291915.title: Mechanism of action of soybean oil in arthropods: mortality results from tracheal infiltration and obstruction of gas exchange structures
pmc-13291915.creator: Ricardo Castro-Torres, Jorge Valdez-Carrasco, Esteban Rodríguez-Leyva, Lauro Soto-Rojas, J Refugio Lomeli-Flores
pmc-13291915.description: Oils are widely used in arthropod pest control, yet their modes of action remain poorly understood and often differ across studies. To investigate the mechanism of action of a commercial soybean oil formulation, we evaluated its physical and toxicological effects on three arthropod species across several developmental stages: adults and nymphs of Uroleucon sonchi (L.

pmc-13343506.title: Intracranial Human BT12 Glioblastoma Xenograft is [18F]FET PET Negative but 6‑[18F]Fluoronicotinic Acid PET Positive: Exploring a Novel Approach for Clinical Glioblastoma Imaging
pmc-13343506.creator: David Ekwe, Abiodun Ayo, Xiaoqing Zhuang, Pyry Dillemuth, Tomi T. Airenne, Emel Bakay, Petter Lövdahl, Jonne Kunnas, Lu Bai, Johan Rajander, Tiina A. Salminen, Jessica M. Rosenholm, Pirjo Laakkonen, Xiang-Guo Li
pmc-13343506.description: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults with a median survival of less than 2 years. Radiolabeled amino acids like O-(2-[18F]­fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine ([18F]­FET) have tremendous value in the diagnosis and treatment monitoring of gliomas with positron emission tomography (PET). However, the existence of [18F]­FET PET negativity in 10–30% of patients with glioma underscores the need for alternative radiotracers.

uslaw-usc-t12-s5005.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s5005.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 50 (Check Truncation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Indemnity A reconverting bank and each bank that subsequently transfers, presents, or returns a substitute check in any electronic or paper form, and receives consideration for such transfer, presentment, or return shall indemnify the transferee, any subsequent collecting or returning bank, the depositary bank.
